gloss: salad oil; cooking oil; vegetable oil

definitions.gloss: salad oil; cooking oil; vegetable oil
definitions.explanation: A refined, neutral-flavored vegetable oil used for everyday cooking. In Japan, this is the standard general-purpose cooking oil, typically made from rapeseed (canola), soybean, or a blend.

examples.japanese: フライパンにサラダ{油|あぶら}をひく。
examples.english: Coat the frying pan with cooking oil.

examples.japanese: サラダ{油|あぶら}が{切|き}れたから{買|か}ってきて。
examples.english: We're out of cooking oil, so please go buy some.

examples.japanese: {揚|あ}げ{物|もの}にはサラダ{油|あぶら}よりも{米油|こめあぶら}のほうがカラッと{揚|あ}がる。
examples.english: Rice bran oil gives a crispier result for deep-frying than salad oil.

notes:
The most common general-purpose cooking oil in Japanese kitchens. The name "salad oil" comes from the fact that it is refined enough to be used in cold dressings without solidifying, but it is used for all cooking purposes including stir-frying and deep-frying.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- サラダ{油|あぶら}をひく: to coat with oil
- サラダ{油|あぶら}で{炒|いた}める: to stir-fry in cooking oil
- サラダ{油|あぶら}{大|おお}さじ1: 1 tablespoon of cooking oil

OTHER COOKING OILS:
- ごま{油|あぶら}: sesame oil — for flavoring
- オリーブオイル: olive oil
- {米油|こめあぶら}: rice bran oil — increasingly popular
- {揚|あ}げ{油|あぶら}: deep-frying oil

USAGE:
Despite the name "salad," this oil is rarely used just for salads in modern Japan. It is the default cooking oil, equivalent to "vegetable oil" in English-speaking countries.
